source.title: Arte de projetar em arquitetura
source.author: Ernst Neufert
source.edition: Portuguese, translated from the 21st German edition, Editorial Gustavo Gili
source.pages: book_page = printed page number; pdf_page = page in the 450-page scan (book_page + 17)
source.note: Paraphrased dimensional facts for reference. No text, figures or scans from the book are reproduced. Check current local codes before building.

body.reference_height_modulor.rule: The Le Corbusier Modulor uses a 1.829 m standing figure, with navel height at 1.130 m.

body.arm_outstretched_one_side.rule: With one arm stretched out sideways, a standing person needs about 1.125 m of width.

body.bending_forward_footprint.rule: Bending forward from the waist takes about 0.875 m of floor depth, and the top of the bent back is about 1.375 m above the floor.

body.shoulder_width.rule: Plan for about 0.50 m across the shoulders of a standing adult.

body.standing_depth_profile.rule: Seen from the side, a standing body is about 0.30 m deep.

body.standing_height_reach_horizontal.rule: A standing adult is shown as 1.75 m tall, with the arm held level at about 1.50 m and needing 0.875 m of depth.

lying.bed_length.rule: A person lying flat needs 2.00 m of length; the body itself measures about 1.875 m.

lying.sitting_up_in_bed_headroom.rule: Sitting upright on a mattress takes about 0.875 m of headroom above the mattress and about 1.25 m of length.

sitting.armchair_depth.rule: A lounge armchair with its user needs about 1.25 m of depth, with the seat at 0.25 to 0.35 m and a side table about 0.625 m high.

sitting.dining_table_height.rule: A dining table stands about 0.75 m high, with the seat at 0.40 to 0.45 m and a footprint about 0.875 m deep.

sitting.seated_head_height.rule: A person seated at a work chair reaches about 1.35 m to the top of the head.

sitting.work_table_height.rule: A desk for seated work stands 0.75 to 0.80 m high, with the chair seat at 0.45 to 0.48 m and a total depth of about 0.875 m.

reach.arms_spread.rule: Arms spread fully sideways span about 1.75 m, which is less than the 2.35 m inside width of a container.

reach.overhead_vertical.rule: With the arm raised straight up, a standing person reaches about 2.25 m. A finished container interior is often below 2.39 m once floor and ceiling build-up is added, so overhead storage and fixtures may sit within reach or bring the ceiling close to the head.

reach.working_at_counter.rule: Leaning over a counter to work takes about 1.125 m of floor depth, with the outstretched hand at about 1.50 m. Reaching up over a 0.50 m deep counter reaches about 2.0 m, in a total depth of about 0.875 m.

circulation.moving_allowance.rule: For people who are walking rather than standing, add at least 10% to these widths.

circulation.single_person.rule: One person standing face-on between two walls needs about 0.625 m of width.

circulation.single_person_arms_akimbo.rule: One person with elbows out or legs apart needs about 0.875 m between walls.

circulation.single_person_sideways.rule: The absolute minimum gap a person can turn sideways and squeeze through is about 0.375 m.

circulation.step_length.rule: A normal walking step is about 0.75 m long, and a marching step about 0.875 m.

circulation.three_people.rule: Three people abreast need about 1.70 m, and four need about 2.25 m.

circulation.two_people.rule: Two people side by side need about 1.00 m between walls, or about 1.15 m if one carries a bag.

circulation.with_two_suitcases.rule: A person carrying a bag in each hand needs about 1.00 m of width; with one bag, about 0.80 m.

occupancy.max_density.rule: The tightest crowding possible is about 6 standing people per square metre, as in a cable car.

vehicle.aisle_width.rule: Aisles in compact coach interiors are drawn about 0.60 to 0.70 m wide.

vehicle.compact_seat_area.rule: A dense rail-bus layout gives about 0.45 m2 of floor per seat; a 2nd-class express coach gives about 1.05 m2.

vehicle.door_height_width.rule: Train compartment doors are 1.8 to 2.0 m high and 0.60 to 0.70 m wide, a workable minimum for tight interiors.

door.clear_opening_wood_frame.rule: Inside a wood frame, the clear opening is about 50 mm less than the rough size, e.g. 825 × 1975 mm for an 875 × 2000 mm opening.

door.double_leaf_widths.rule: Double-leaf door openings are 1250, 1500 or 1750 mm wide.

door.floor_gap.rule: Leave about 7.5 mm between the floor and the bottom of the door leaf.

door.handle_height.rule: Put the door handle centre 1.05 m above the floor.

door.hinge_positions.value: 250 mm below head, 300 mm above floor
door.hinge_positions.rule: Centre the top hinge 250 mm below the frame head and the bottom hinge 300 mm above the floor.

door.interior_single_leaf.rule: Single-leaf interior doors are drawn at 750, 875 or 1000 mm wide by 2000 mm high; cellar and secondary doors use 625–875 × 1875 mm.

door.module_heights.rule: Doors in the main rooms take a 2000 mm high rough opening; cellar and secondary doors can use 1875 mm.

door.module_widths.rule: Single-leaf door rough openings come in 125 mm steps: 625, 750, 875 or 1000 mm wide.

door.overhead_folding_recess.value: 25–30 cm lintel recess; 32 cm ceiling track
door.overhead_folding_recess.rule: In tight spots with no room to slide sideways, a door that folds up into the lintel needs about 25–30 cm of space above the opening.

window.head_to_ceiling.rule: In the sketches, the window head sits about 20 to 50 cm below the ceiling.

window.sill_height_desk.rule: In living rooms and studies, set the sill at desk height of about 78 cm.

window.sill_height_kitchen.rule: In kitchens, the window is drawn above the worktop backsplash with a sill of about 1.25 m.

window.sill_height_low_view.rule: A low sill of about 50 cm suits rooms that sit high with a good view, so seated people can see out. It is a low option, not a minimum sill height. Below standard sill height, check guarding and fall-protection rules.

window.sill_height_office.rule: In offices, the sketch shows a 1.00 m sill with about 1.50 m of glazing above it.

ramp.comfortable_slope.rule: Walking ramps feel comfortable at gradients between 1:10 and 1:8.

stair.going_minus_rise.rule: The most comfortable steps have a tread about 12 cm deeper than the riser is tall.

stair.handrail_walkline_narrow.rule: On narrow or curved stairs, put the walking line 35–40 cm in from the handrail.

stair.handrail_walkline_straight.rule: On comfortable straight flights, the walking line runs about 55 cm from the handrail.

stair.nosing_overhang.rule: Each tread's nosing should stick out 2 to 5 cm past the riser below.

stair.optimal_step.rule: The best step is a 17 cm riser with a 29 cm tread.

stair.rise_going_alt_formula.rule: A less common check is that one riser plus one tread equals about 48 cm.

stair.rise_going_formula.rule: Size steps so that two risers plus one tread fall between 61 and 64 cm, ideally about 62.5 cm.

stair.ship_ladder_max_pitch.rule: Ship-type stairs can be as steep as a 21/15 riser/tread with no rail, or 25/10 if they have a handrail.

stair.spiral_min_tread.value: ≥10 cm at 15 cm from the narrow end
stair.spiral_min_tread.rule: On spiral stairs, measured 15 cm from the narrow end, the tread must still be at least 10 cm deep.

stair.step_normal_range.rule: Standard steps for homes and offices use 16–17 cm risers and 29–30 cm treads.

stair.width_three_persons.rule: Three people walking side by side need about 1.875 m of stair width.

stair.width_two_pass.rule: For two people to pass each other, the stair needs at least about 1.10 m of width; the drawing shows 1.25 m.

ramp.slope_classes.rule: Up to 6° (1:10) a ramp counts as flat, 1:10 to 1:6 as gentle, and 1:6 to 1:2.5 as steep.

stair.compact_1m_plan_area.value: ≈4.2–5.2 m² for 2.75 m storey, 1.0 m wide
stair.compact_1m_plan_area.rule: A 1.0 m wide flight with no landing covering a 2.75 m storey (16 steps of about 17/29) takes roughly 4.2 to 5.2 m² of floor area.

stair.flight_step_count.rule: A single flight should have at least 3 and no more than 18 steps.

stair.headroom_attic_drawing.rule: The section drawings show at least 1.95 m of clear headroom at the base of the stair and under an attic roof.

stair.headroom_dwelling_min.rule: In homes, headroom over a stair must be more than 1.80 m.

stair.headroom_general.rule: Headroom over a stair is usually 2.1 m.

stair.landing_depth.rule: Make a landing a whole number of 63 cm strides plus one tread deep, e.g. 92 cm, or 1.55 m for two strides.

stair.landing_door_swing.rule: A door that opens onto a landing must not swing into the landing's area.

stair.landing_width.rule: A landing must be at least as wide as the stair itself.

stair.max_pitch_multi_family.rule: Stairs in multi-storey housing should be no steeper than about a 20/23 riser/tread.

stair.max_pitch_single_family.rule: In single-family homes, a stair can be as steep as a 20 cm riser over a 20 cm tread.

stair.width_attic_cellar_rental.rule: Cellar and attic stairs in rented houses can be 70 cm wide with a pitch of up to 45°.

stair.width_multi_family.rule: In multi-family housing, stairs are generally at least 1.0 m wide. The footnote applies this to buildings with more than two full storeys.

stair.width_single_family.rule: In single-family homes, stairs need at least 90 cm clear between the handrail and the wall.

ladder.attic_folding_hatch.value: hatch 0.85–1.45 m long; at 2.10 m ceiling needs 1.30–1.90 m swing space
ladder.attic_folding_hatch.rule: With a 2.10 m ceiling, a folding attic ladder needs a hatch 0.85 to 1.45 m long and 1.30 to 1.90 m of space in the loft for the fold.

ladder.fixed_rung_spacing.rule: The fixed ladder drawing shows rungs about 31 cm apart and about 1.00 m of clear space in front.

stair.furniture_transport.rule: To carry furniture of about 2.00 × 0.70 m up a stair, the landing needs about 1.40 m.

stair.well_gap_min.rule: Between two parallel flights, leave a gap of at least 12 cm to fix the balustrade.

kitchen.width_min.rule: Plan a kitchen no narrower than 1.875 m; the Frankfurt kitchen uses this as its minimum width.

kitchen.auxiliary_counter.depth.rule: Secondary or auxiliary work surfaces can be just 45 cm deep.

kitchen.counter.depth.rule: Kitchen worktops should be 55 to 65 cm deep.

kitchen.counter.height.rule: The usual worktop height is 85 cm, which suits both kneading and dishwashing.

kitchen.counter.height_range.rule: Section drawings show worktops from 75 cm to 90 cm high. 85 cm is the height recommended for both kneading and washing up.

kitchen.extract_duct.diameter.rule: Where there is no flue, an extractor duct of about 275 mm diameter can take fumes out.

kitchen.hood.height_above_hob.rule: Mount the extractor hood at least 65 cm above the cooking surface.

kitchen.oven.clear_front.rule: An oven or pull-out grill under the range needs about 1.10 m clear in front for bending and handling.

kitchen.room_height.rule: Kitchen sections draw tall units and shelving up to about 2.10 m. This is the height of the cabinetry, not a minimum ceiling height.

kitchen.seated_work.height.rule: Provide a pull-out board at about 65 cm under the 85 cm counter for working seated.

kitchen.swing_door.width.rule: A swing door between kitchen and dining is shown about 1.00 m wide, with a kick plate up to 40 cm.

kitchen.two_line.aisle_small.rule: In a small two-line kitchen 2.25 m wide, leave 1.00 to 1.10 m between the 75 cm and 50 cm deep runs so a second person can help.

kitchen.two_line.width_small.rule: A small kitchen with counters on both walls can work at 2.25 m wide overall.

kitchen.two_person.width.rule: A two-person kitchen section is 2.50 m wide: 45 and 45 cm units, an 85 cm aisle, and a 75 cm range on the opposite wall.

kitchen.wall_cabinet.clear_above_counter.rule: Leave about 50 cm between the 85 cm worktop and the underside of wall cabinets.

kitchen.wall_cabinet.depth.rule: Wall cabinets over a worktop are drawn about 30 cm deep. The 45 cm unit shown is a pass-through cupboard over a serving hatch.

kitchen.wall_cabinet.top_reach.rule: Keep the top shelf of wall cabinets at or below about 1.85 m so it stays reachable.

kitchen.sink.bowl_size.rule: A standard sink bowl is about 43 by 43 cm and 22 cm deep.

kitchen.sink.height.rule: Set the sink at 85 to 90 cm for standing work, or 75 cm with a forward-tilted basin for seated work.

kitchen.stove.footprint.rule: Freestanding ranges take about 55 to 65 cm depth and 55 to 110 cm width, at 80 to 85 cm high.

kitchen.frankfurt.aisle.rule: In the Frankfurt kitchen the clear aisle between the two runs is about 86 cm, and later testing found the room should have been slightly wider.

kitchen.frankfurt.length.rule: The reference Frankfurt kitchen is 1.875 m wide by about 3.44 m long, a galley with counters on both sides.

kitchen.interior_kitchenette.rule: An interior kitchenette with forced ventilation can fit in 1.875 m by 1.25 m.

kitchen.kitchenette.one_person.rule: A one-person apartment kitchenette cabinet fits in a 90 cm wide, 60 cm deep, 2.00 m tall unit.

kitchen.fridge.small.rule: Small refrigerators of 50 to 100 L take about 55 cm width and 55 to 65 cm depth, at 80 to 90 cm high.

kitchen.base_cabinet.dims.rule: Base cabinets are 80 to 90 cm high (85 preferred) and 45 to 60 cm deep.

kitchen.sink_top.depth.rule: Sink tops over built-in cabinets are 55 to 60 cm deep, with 16 to 18 cm deep bowls.

kitchen.tall_cabinet.dims.rule: Tall broom or pantry cabinets are 1.70 to 2.20 m high, 50 to 60 cm wide and 35 to 55 cm deep.

kitchen.toe_kick.height.rule: Give base cabinets a recessed plinth at least 8 cm high, set back 6 to 10 cm, for toes and cleaning.

bath.compact_wc_bath.depth.rule: A compact apartment WC with bathtub fits in about 1.46 m depth, using a 76 cm tub width and a 70 cm WC zone.

bath.tub.width.rule: Compact bathroom plans use a bathtub about 76 cm wide.

bath.wc_plus_basin.width.rule: A separate WC with basin is shown in a 1.00 by 1.25 m cell.

bath.wet_core.width.rule: Bathrooms sharing a plumbing wall with the kitchen are planned at 1.875 m wide by about 2.37 to 2.75 m long.

bed.child_sizes.rule: Children's beds come in 60x125 and 70x140 cm interior sizes.

bed.double_mattress_std.rule: The standardized double bed is 150 cm wide and 200 cm long inside the frame.

bed.exterior_allowance.rule: To get a metal bed's outer footprint, add 6 cm to the inner width and 10 cm to the inner length.

bed.mattress_top_height.rule: The top edge of the bed's wooden mattress frame sits about 40 cm above the floor.

bed.niche_with_overhead_storage.value: 3.26 m wall; bed niche 1.50 m high; seat 30–35 cm
bed.niche_with_overhead_storage.rule: A small-room scheme puts the bed in a niche with cupboards above and beside it, taking up a 3.26 m wall.

bed.single_mattress_std.rule: The standard adult single bed frame is 90 by 190 cm inside; 80x180 and 100x200 are the adult alternatives.

bunk.alcove_with_wardrobe.value: 2.00 m bunk + 1.25 m wardrobe; bunk height 1.50 m; ceiling 2.60 m
bunk.alcove_with_wardrobe.rule: A 2.00 m bunk alcove sits beside a 1.25 m wardrobe. The bunk stack is about 1.50 m high and the drawing assumes a 2.60 m ceiling, so a standard 2.39 m container interior needs a lower stack or a high-cube box.

bed.double_drawn_length.rule: A double bed is drawn at 1.50 m wide by 2.00 m long overall.

bed.gap_between_singles.rule: Two parallel 90 cm single beds are drawn with a 50 cm gap between them.

bed.gap_between_singles_alt.rule: A more generous layout for two single beds leaves an 80 cm walkway between them.

bed.separate_doubles_layout.rule: In one shown layout, two beds placed head to foot in a room fit a 1.40 m bed, an 80 cm aisle and a 90 cm bed across the width.

bed.twin_pushed_together.rule: Two single beds pushed together take up about 1.80 m by 1.90 m.

bunk.tier_spacing.rule: Bunks are drawn with about 90 cm between the levels and the upper bunk at roughly 1.40 m.

wardrobe.depth_built_in.rule: Built-in bedroom wardrobes are drawn 60 cm deep.

wardrobe.depth_shallow_corridor.rule: Wardrobe units that divide two rooms are drawn about 55 cm deep.

wardrobe.partition_thickness.rule: Partitions between wardrobe compartments are 3 to 10 cm thick, depending on how they are built.

wardrobe.walkin_width.rule: A walk-in dressing room for a large house is drawn about 2.80 m by 1.80 m.

aisle.between_shelving.rule: Aisles between shelving units are usually 72 to 77 cm wide, or 85 cm where use is heavy.

shelf.depth_range.rule: Standard shelf depths are 20, 25, 30 or 35 cm, with 15 and 40 cm as exceptions.

shelf.top_reach.rule: The highest shelf you can comfortably reach is at about 1.90 m, on a shelving unit 2.25 m tall.

wardrobe.office_hanging.value: 1.22 m wide, 0.47–0.50 m deep, 2.10 m tall
wardrobe.office_hanging.rule: An office cupboard with a hanging-clothes section is 1.22 m wide, 47 to 50 cm deep and 2.10 m tall.

wardrobe.staff_locker.rule: A clothes locker for staff is about 1.20 m wide, 42 to 50 cm deep and 2.0 to 2.1 m tall.

dining.table_height.rule: Standard dining table height is 78 cm.

dining.table_min_rect.rule: The smallest standard rectangular dining top is 70 by 100 cm.

dining.booth_min.rule: The tightest eating nook, a railway-carriage style booth with fold-down seats, needs about 1.70 by 1.27 m around a 60 cm table.

dining.corner_bench.rule: A corner bench with side cupboards seats a small group compactly in about 1.85 m by 1.95 m.

dining.min_room_6.rule: A minimum dining room for six around a central table is about 3.20 by 3.70 m, with no sideboards.

dining.nook_loose_chairs.rule: The same nook with loose chairs needs slightly more width, about 1.80 by 1.00 m.

dining.round_table_formula.rule: To size a round table, multiply place width by number of seats and divide by pi; six 60 cm places need about 1.04 m.

dining.seat_depth_zone.rule: When service passes behind the chairs, the seated diner takes about 50 cm from the table edge, and the passage starts after that.

dining.table_width.rule: Dining tables run 55 to 110 cm wide, with 10 to 20 cm extra at each end seat.

dining.wall_clearance_no_service.rule: If no one serves at the table, allow 45 to 55 cm from the table edge to the wall. This covers the seated diner, not extra space behind the chair.

dining.wall_clearance_served.rule: When someone serves from behind the chairs, keep 90 cm to 1.00 m clear between the seat zone and the wall.

dining.width_per_place.rule: Give each diner 55 to 70 cm of table edge.

desk.study_carrel.rule: A desk built into shelving is about 1.00 m wide and 65 cm deep.

counter.service.rule: Public service counters are about 62.5 cm deep and 90 cm high, rising to 1 m when only 30 cm deep.

desk.chair_zone.rule: Allow 45 to 70 cm behind the desk for a swivel chair, which takes up roughly 1.05 to 1.33 m².

desk.compact.rule: A compact office desk of 140 by 70 cm, 76 cm high, saves about 0.5 m² over the standard desk.

desk.standard.rule: The standard office desk measures 156 by 78 cm and stands 78 cm high.

cleaning_cabinet.depth.rule: A broom or cleaning cupboard is about 37.5 cm deep and 1.80 m tall, from 37.5 cm wide upward.

laundry.ironing.board_size.rule: An ironing board is about 1.70 m long, 30 to 42 cm wide, at roughly 85 cm high.

laundry.foldaway_ironing.cabinet.rule: A fold-down ironing table recessed in the wall needs a cabinet about 45 cm wide, 15 cm deep and 2.25 m tall.

laundry.ironing.height_standing.rule: Ironing standing needs a board about 90 cm high; seated ironing works at about 65 cm.

pantry.headroom.rule: Pantries and storerooms may be under 2.50 m high but need at least 1.90 m standing height, ideally 2.00 m.

air.co2_per_person.value: 0.020 m3/h CO2 and 40 g/h water vapour
air.co2_per_person.rule: An average person gives off about 0.020 m3 of CO2 and 40 g of water vapour per hour.

air.natural_change_rate.rule: In detached buildings, natural infiltration gives roughly 1.5 to 2 air changes per hour even with the windows shut.

air.reduced_volume_high_ventilation.rule: With strong ventilation, such as open windows or mechanical air, the volume per person can drop to 7.5 m3, or 10 m3 in bedrooms.

air.room_volume_per_adult.rule: Natural air changes of 1.5 to 2 per hour are enough when each adult has 16 to 24 m3 of room volume, or each child 8 to 12 m3.

air.volume_assumed_ceiling_height.rule: The 16 to 24 m3 per adult figure assumes a clear height of at least 2.5 m, which works out to 6.4 to 9.6 m2 of floor per adult. At 2.39 m inside, a container needs more floor per person to reach the same volume.

air.volume_per_adult_one_change.rule: To keep CO2 below 1 part per thousand, each adult needs 32 m3 of fresh air per hour, and each child 14 m3.

ventilation.opening_geometry.rule: For the same area, tall narrow openings move more air than low wide ones. An inlet near the floor paired with an outlet near the ceiling is more effective.

ventilation.room_humidity_table.value: living 20 C/65%, bedroom 18 C/55%, kitchen 20 C/75%, bath 22 C/80%
ventilation.room_humidity_table.rule: Design conditions by room: living rooms 20 C at 65% RH, bedrooms 18 C at 55%, kitchens 20 C at 75%, bathrooms 22 C at 80%.

ventilation.stack_height.rule: Stack-driven airflow depends on the height difference between the inlet and outlet openings, not on the length of the duct.

ventilation.windows_sufficient_dwellings.rule: Ventilating through windows is generally enough for living spaces; sash windows work best, letting air in low and out high.

daylight.design_outdoor_lux.rule: Size windows against a minimum outdoor level of 3000 lux on the horizontal; the CIE suggests 5000 lux.

daylight.room_efficiency.rule: Rooms with vertical windows deliver 30 to 50% of the entering light to the work plane; use 40% as the default.

daylight.window_to_floor_basic.rule: Window area equal to 1/8 of the floor gives only about 45 lux on average, which is enough just for coarse work.

daylight.window_to_floor_drawing.rule: Fine work needing 150 lux calls for window area of about 42% of the floor, assuming 3000 lux outside, a window factor of 0.3 and 40% efficiency.

daylight.work_plane_height.rule: Daylight calculations measure light on a horizontal work plane 1 m above the floor.

lighting.cove_gap_to_ceiling.rule: For indirect cove lighting, keep the gap between the cove and the ceiling at least 1/8 of the room width so the ceiling is lit evenly.

lighting.wall_reflectance.value: white plaster ~86%, white oil paint 76%, light yellow 55%
lighting.wall_reflectance.rule: Light finishes reflect much more light than dark ones: white plaster about 86%, white oil paint 76%, light yellow 55%, against roughly 4 to 13% for black and saturated reds. Our inference: this favours light finishes in a small interior.

climate.heat_per_adult.rule: An adult gives off about 96 kcal/h at rest, 118 kcal/h in normal work and 140 kcal/h in heavy work, which matters for cooling a small box.

climate.relative_humidity.rule: Keep indoor relative humidity near 50 to 60%, and always between 40 and 70%.

climate.room_temperature.rule: Aim for 18 to 20 C for people at rest and 15 to 18 C for active work.

climate.summer_indoor_temp.value: e.g. 25 C inside at 30 C outside
climate.summer_indoor_temp.rule: In summer, the most comfortable indoor temperature rises with the outdoor one, from 20 C at 20 C outside to 28 C at 36 C outside.
